```javascript
// Kyverno policy (as YAML in practice)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-privileged-containers
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: check-secctx
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet","Job"]
    validate:
      message: "Container must drop ALL capabilities, run as non-root, and readOnly rootfs"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop:
                    - ALL
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design end-to-end supply chain controls for Helm charts in a multi-tenant environment, including signature provenance, SBOM coverage, and admission-time enforcement. It also probes per-tenant key management and how to demonstrate both failing and passing cases.

## Key Concepts
- Helm chart signing with cosign
- SBOM generation for chart dependencies
- Rekor attestations
- Kyverno/OPA admission policies
- Tenant-specific key management and verification
- Local and CI verification workflows

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal GitHub Actions gate (high level)
name: Sign and Verify Helm Chart
on: [push]
jobs:
  sign-verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Set up cosign
        run: cosign version
      - name: Sign chart
        run: cosign sign --key cosign-keys/${{ env.TENANT }}.key charts/myapp-0.1.0.tgz
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: syft chart:charts/myapp-0.1.0.tgz -o cyclonedx-json
      - name: Rekor attestation
        run: cosign attach to Rekor
      - name: Publish verification results
        run: echo verified
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate tenant keys with minimal blast radius?
- What are failure modes if the SBOM is missing or signatures don’t verify?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to combine SBOM provenance, cryptographic attestation, and admission control in multi-tenant Kubernetes environments with concrete artifacts and workflow.

## Key Concepts
- SBOM provenance (CycloneDX)
- Cosign signatures and Rekor attestations
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Rego policy validation for image attestation and CVE severity

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: ImageSBOMAttestation
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: ImageSBOMAttestation
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package imagesbomattestation
      
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
        container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        not valid_image(container.image)
        msg := sprintf("Container image %v fails SBOM/attestation validation", [container.image])
      }
      
      valid_image(image) {
        has_attestation(image)
        no_high_severity_vulns(image)
      }
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement a basic software supply chain gate: SBOM generation and vulnerability scanning integrated into CI, with clear pass/fail criteria.

- SBOM generation with Syft
- Vulnerability scanning with Trivy

## Code Example

```yaml
name: SBOM and vulnerability gate
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: docker build -t service:latest .
      - name: Generate SBOM
        uses: anchore/syft-action@v0
        with:
          image: service:latest
      - name: Trivy scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@v0
        with:
          image: service:latest
          severity: HIGH,CRITICAL
          format: table
          exit-code: 1
```

```dockerfile
# Failing Dockerfile (vulnerable)
FROM debian:stretch-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
```

```dockerfile
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
```

## Why This Question Is Asked
This tests practical policy design, edge-case handling, and CI integration for Kubernetes manifests in a multi-team environment. Candidates must demonstrate understanding of resource isolation, pod hardening, network security, and hardware scheduling constraints.

## Key Concepts
- **ResourceQuota and LimitRange**: Prevent resource starvation and enforce default resource requests/limits per namespace
- **Pod securityContext**: Enforce runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and capability dropping for workload hardening
- **Ingress TLS with cert-manager**: Ensure encrypted external traffic with automated certificate management
- **GPU scheduling constraints**: Use nodeSelector and resource requests to restrict GPU workloads to approved namespaces and nodes
- **CI validation**: Integrate Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper with kubectl dry-run for pre-merge enforcement

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy for ML Platform Gates
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-platform-gates
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
    - name: require-resource-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Namespace]
      validate:
        message: "Each namespace must have a ResourceQuota."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              quota-ready: "true"

    - name: require-security-context
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      validate:
        message: "Containers must run as non-root with read-only filesystem and drop ALL capabilities."
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: [ALL]

    - name: require-ingress-tls
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Ingress]
      validate:
        message: "Ingress must use TLS with cert-manager annotation."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              (cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer): "?*"
          spec:
            tls:
              - secretName: "?*"

    - name: gpu-in-approved-namespaces
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      preconditions:
        - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
          operator: In
          value: ["1", "2", "4"]
      validate:
        message: "GPU pods are only allowed in approved namespaces with nvidia nodeSelector."
        pattern:
          spec:
            nodeSelector:
              nvidia.com/gpu: "?*"
```

```bash
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Dry-run validate manifests

kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest manifest.yaml
```

**CI Integration (GitHub Actions):**
```yaml
name: Manifest Validation
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate with Kyverno
        run: |
          kyverno apply cluster-policy.yaml \
            --manifest manifests/ \
            --policy-report \
            --fail-only-on-exists
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical policy enforcement for serverless workloads in enterprise environments, focusing on outbound access control, SPIFFE identity management, and namespace-scoped allowlists within Knative platforms.

## Key Concepts

- SPIFFE ID-based access control for function isolation
- Namespace-scoped allowlists for Pub/Sub topics and storage buckets
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate with Rego policy validation
- Kyverno ClusterPolicy as alternative enforcement mechanism
- End-to-end testing with compliant and noncompliant deployment scenarios

## Code Examples

The implementation demonstrates enterprise-grade security patterns for serverless architectures, showing how major organizations can enforce zero-trust networking principles while maintaining operational flexibility through declarative policy enforcement.
